page: Google Cloud Platform n2-highcpu-96 is an x86_64 architecture server powered by an Intel Xeon processor running at 2.6 GHz. It features 96 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 48 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, providing two threads per core. The system is equipped with 96.0 GB of RAM, resulting in a resource density of 1.0 GB of memory per core. Cache resources include 48 KB of L1d cache, 1 MB of L2 cache, and 54 MB of L3 cache. No local storage or GPUs are bundled with this instance type, and it includes zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark results indicate strong multi-core performance, with stress-ng multi-core CPU and PassMark CPU scores placing in the top 25% of tested systems. The processor supports advanced instruction sets including AVX, AVX-512 Foundation, and AVX-512 Vector Neural Network Instructions, which contribute to strong performance in specialized tasks such as software compilation, ray tracing, and image processing. Memory bandwidth is also highly rated, with read-only small block cached bandwidth reaching 4889.85 GB/sec and uncached large block write bandwidth at 137.15 GB/sec. Single-core performance and text processing benchmarks fall within the average range.

Given its high vCPU count relative to memory, this server is optimized for compute-heavy workloads that do not require massive RAM footprints. It demonstrates strong throughput for static web serving and high-volume database operations, as well as rapid Redis SET operations. The instance is well-suited for parallelized tasks such as software compilation, image processing, ray tracing, and high-throughput web serving. However, the 1.0 GB per core memory allocation represents a tradeoff for memory-intensive database systems or large-scale in-memory caching.
